title: Cheshire (pulp-platform/cheshire)
_note: PULP's Linux-capable host SoC, plus the dependency IP that is not already a
family of its own: the AXI last-level cache, the AXI real-time unit, atomics
and stream adapters, the AXI VGA controller, CLIC and CLINT, the iDMA engine,
the interrupt router, the OBI fabric and peripherals, the vendored OpenTitan
peripherals, the serial link, unbent, the APB UART and the DRAM simulation
model.
Its closure is Bender's, resolved by the SHARED test/ext_ip/bender_setup.sh
that pulpissimo uses -- bender installed as a prebuilt binary, `bender
checkout` honouring the checked-in Bender.lock so all 26 dependencies are
pinned, and .bender_resolved/<package> symlinks so the hash-suffixed
checkout directories do not leak into roots and incdirs.
Cheshire needed NO per-dependency patching, unlike pulpissimo (whose
adv_dbg_if ships a trailing comma in its own file list) -- evidence that the
comma is one dependency's sloppiness rather than a Bender-wide problem.  The
script's comma fix is generic and simply finds nothing to do here.
sweep_paths covers cheshire's own hw/ and the new packages only: axi,
common_cells, cva6 (its own family), fpnew (swept as cvfpu),
register_interface, apb, tech_cells_generic, common_verification, riscv-dbg
and fpu_div_sqrt_mvp (both swept under pulpissimo) stay available to every
closure but are not counted twice.
exclude_srcs drops the VERIFICATION sources Bender lists as part of a
package: axi/src/axi_test.sv describes itself as 'a set of testbench
utilities for AXI interfaces' and uses queues with `%h`, which read_slang
rejects (`value of type 'logic[7:0]$[$]' is invalid for '%h'`) -- and because
it landed in every closure it cost every row its reference.  The axi family
itself never trips this because its own closure does not pull the file.  axi_slave_compare.sv goes with it: it is the only file that imports axi_test, and is itself a verification comparator.
First local sweep 2026-10-28, WITH the `bind` section (266 rows): 97 / 139
comparable proven, 123 / 139 elaborate, 98 co-sim PASS, 169 rows with 0
undriven, 1.3 h of row time.
What `bind` is worth, measured on the same 266 rows:
unbound   bound
comparable rows           78     139
formally proven           62      97
skip (default params)    158      82
co-sim PASS               61      98
rows with 0 undriven     102     169
`differs` (new leads)      5      18
76 rows left the skip bucket, 61 more became comparable, 35 more are proven,
and 13 formal-only `differs` rows that were previously INVISIBLE are now
visible -- a row that skips can never surface a defect, so those matter as
much as the proven count.
How it binds, and three things that cost a measurement each:
* The types come from each package's OWN typedef macros (axi/typedef.svh,
register_interface/typedef.svh, obi/typedef.svh), not hand-written
structs, so the shapes stay in step with upstream.
* RULE ORDER matters: the obi_* rules sit BEFORE the generic
`(^|_)req_t$` / `rsp_t$` ones.  Behind them, `sbr_port_obi_req_t` is bound
to an AXI type and obi_mux fails with `no member named 'req'`.
* Three rules map to NULL, which DECLINES to bind: iDMA's internal datapath
types (r_dp_req_t / w_dp_req_t and their responses, the meta channels,
idma_mut_tf_opt_t) are generated per configuration inside the backend and
carry members -- `offset`, `tailer`, an `axi` wrapper -- that no shared
macro describes.  Bound by the generic rule they fail with
`no member named 'offset'`, which reads as a read_slang limitation and is
really the wrapper's fault; declined, the row reports an honest
`skip (defaults don't elaborate)`.  Inventing those structs would mean
measuring a netlist built from a shape nobody verified.
* An iDMA PRELUDE was tried and reverted: `IDMA_TYPEDEF_FULL_REQ_T` expands
to types referencing `idma_pkg`, which is not in the closure of a row that
has nothing to do with iDMA -- so it made EVERY bound row fail with
`unknown class or package 'idma_pkg'`, including axi_vga and obi_err_sbr
which the AXI / OBI rules had just turned green.  A prelude is shared by
every wrapper in the family, so it may only name types every closure can
see.  Caught by re-probing two known-good rows, not by the aggregate.
82 rows still skip: iDMA's declined datapath types, axi_llc's `desc_t` /
`way_inp_t`, and a CVA6 FP-format enum (`member 'XF8ALT' is not covered by
any assignment`).
exclude_srcs also drops idma/target/rtl/idma_generated.sv: an AGGREGATE of 39
modules and packages the checkout also ships individually, so compiling both
gave `duplicate definition of 'idma_desc64_reg_pkg'` and cost 14 rows their
reference.  The individual files are kept -- they make better rows anyway.
Leads worth working, in order:
* apb_uart: `differs` with 5 slang-clean co-simulated divergences -- the
cleanest reader lead here.
* idma_mp_midend_synth: `differs` with 2 slang-clean divergences.
* obi_uart_tx: proven only to seq 4 and the co-sim diverges deeper (8
cycles), slang clean -- a miter-depth row, like VeeR EH2's
eh2_ifu_mem_ctl.
* the seven idma_backend_synth_* rows diverge by ~275 cycles each but have
NO read_slang reference (duplicate-definition errors in the iDMA package),
so they are unadjudicated -- give them an oracle before chasing them, the
NVDLA lesson.
* cheshire_soc_regs, clint_reg and slink_reg are `differs` with no co-sim
divergence: formal-only, register-file shapes.
